source.title: From Isolation to Entanglement: When Do Interpretability Methods Identify and Disentangle Known Concepts?
source.authors: Aaron Mueller; Andrew Lee; Shruti B. Joshi; E. Lubana; Dhanya Sridhar; P. Reizinger

record.file_problem: not stated; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The study evaluates SAE and probe representations and reports results that qualify claims about feature completeness, recoverability, and one-dimensional concept representation. It finds that correlational disentanglement does not guarantee selective steering.
record.gate_note: The paper measures concept recoverability, feature splitting, and effects of steering features on multiple concepts. It also tests whether sparse probes need more than one feature dimension. It does not test sparse-overcomplete toy networks, feature sparsity/importance trade-offs, or the superposition geometry in the claim. SAE reconstruction metrics and cited results from other studies are not cataloged as claim results.
record.test_reason: Frozen Pythia-70M and Gemma-2-2B were probed with SAEs on PCFG sentences labelled with four known concepts. SAEs recover the concepts better than the raw residual basis, which bears on V4. Concepts are split across many SAE latents and steering one latent moves several concepts, which bears on V5. It is a different method from the toy-model original, and its results qualify V5.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors also stress that SAEs improve on the native neuron basis but are clearly worse than supervised probes. Identifiability failures stem from feature splitting rather than entangled latents. Correlational disentanglement and disjointness do not imply selective steering.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses PCFG-generated labeled sentences, frozen pretrained language models, SAE architectures and probes, correlational metrics, and steering interventions. It does not use the original toy-model superposition setup or its sparsity/importance sweeps.
record.method_sensitivity: Outcomes vary with SAE architecture, model, concept correlations in the featurizer training data, and feature-selection method for steering (activation correlation versus gradient attribution). The authors report generally lower feature selectivity and concept independence with gradient-attribution feature selection.

fits_no_version.finding: Steering pairs of SAE latents gives additive effects (R² 0.98–1.00, Table 2). The latents are disjoint even though they are not selective.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SAE latents act through non-interacting (disjoint) mechanisms, yet each still affects multiple concepts.

record.peer_reviewed: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics
record.problems: The authors state that the PCFG dataset is much narrower than typical SAE training or evaluation distributions, includes only four concepts, and considers only categorical concepts. Some core results are presented in figures without exact values in the text. SAE architectures use different layers in some experiments.
record.rows_left_out: The paper also reports detailed MCC curves and results for alternate concept correlations (Figures 2 and 17), feature-selection steering heatmaps (Figures 4, 13–15), disjointness results (Table 2 and Figures 5 and 16), and qualitative generations (Figure 18). These were not extracted as separate rows where they did not add a distinct result for the listed claim versions beyond the recovery, completeness, steering-selectivity, and dimensionality results above. No study result rows were omitted due to the 60-row limit.

untested.parts: No toy networks, sparsity sweep, phase transition or geometry.
No test of capacity competition or of dedicated versus shared dimensions.
No test of non-capacity causes of polysemanticity.
Recovery is tested only for four researcher-defined categorical concepts on narrow PCFG text. There is no census of naturally occurring features, and no MLP-neuron analysis.
No test of stability across training runs or dictionary sizes, or of canonicality across methods (beyond 3-seed std bands).
Not tested. The 'one-dimension' experiment concerns the number of SAE latents per concept, not the intrinsic dimensionality of the model's features.

missing.what: MCC results when past tense is correlated with passive voice. Natural SAEs are far better at tense=past, especially for Gemma.
Steering with latents chosen by gradient attribution gives slightly lower selectivity and independence and larger ΔLogOdds.
Gemma latents appear less independent than Pythia's in the steering heatmaps.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's V6 link is wrong: the k-sparse experiment counts SAE latents per binary concept, and near-perfect single-direction residual probes (Fig. 9) argue against multi-dimensionality in h. Those rows are relinked to V5 (feature splitting). The 'Neuron' baseline is the residual stream, not MLP neurons. SAEs were trained on different layers (middle layer; final layer for SSAEs), which the authors flag as a confound.

versions.untested_parts: No toy networks with more sparse features than dimensions, feature sparsity or importance sweep, overlap geometry, or sparsity-dependent transition is tested.
The paper does not test whether neuron polysemanticity is caused by capacity competition, or whether important features get dedicated dimensions while other features share.
It does not test whether polysemantic neurons arise through mechanisms other than capacity pressure.

The study tests recovery and distribution of known concepts using SAEs and probes on PCFG-generated sentences processed by Pythia-70M and Gemma-2-2B. It does not establish the same findings for naturally occurring features across broad natural-text distributions or across LLMs generally.

It measures feature completeness and steering selectivity, but does not test whether SAE features are stable across training runs, checkpoints, or methods, or whether they are canonical units of the model.
It tests whether one feature dimension suffices to recover concepts from SAE feature spaces. It does not test whether superposition itself consists geometrically of one-dimensional directions.

rows.subject: Pythia-70M
rows.operation_detail: Measured MCC for known concepts using probes and SAE feature representations as training-data concept correlations varied.
rows.value: The text reports that probes significantly outperform SAEs up to correlations of 0.9; SSAEs perform best or close to best among (S)SAEs. Synthetic-data SAEs achieve performance comparable to Natural SAEs; SSAEs outperform both for Pythia-70M.
rows.uncertainty: Figure 2 shaded regions represent 1 std. dev. across 3 training seeds; individual values are figure-only.
rows.note: The text gives qualitative comparisons rather than exact MCC values. Recovery is demonstrated for controlled PCFG concepts, not a general census of natural-language features.

rows.subject: Gemma-2-2B
rows.operation_detail: Trained k-sparse probes on SAE feature representations while varying k.
rows.measure: MCC as probe feature count increases
rows.baseline: Full probe can use the entire residual vector; exact value not stated.
rows.value: For Top-K, SpADE, SSAE, and Natural, correlation coefficients tend to converge around 10 dimensions; these methods recover most of the performance of a non-sparse probe using the entire residual vector.
rows.uncertainty: Figure values are not stated in text.
rows.note: The study describes this as evidence that one-dimensionality assumptions may yield suboptimal results.
rows.check: k-sparse probes count how many SAE latents a concept needs (about 10). That is feature splitting, a V5 completeness question. It does not test whether the model's own features are multi-dimensional (V6). Single linear probes on the residual stream reach near-perfect accuracy (Fig. 9), which is consistent with 1-D directions in h.

rows.value: ReLU SAEs do not begin saturating even at 10–50 features.
rows.uncertainty: Figure values are not stated in text.
rows.note: More than one feature dimension is useful in this evaluation.
rows.check: Relink from V6 to V5. ReLU SAE probe performance does not saturate even at 10–50 latents, so no small set of latents captures the concept.

source_check.notes: The supplied text is arXiv v2 dated 10 June 2026. DCI completeness concerns concentration of external concept information across latents; it is not dictionary coverage. The r5 note's dimensionality cross-reference should point to r31/r32/r34.

statements.correction: Both models: low DCI completeness; widespread feature splitting; high informativeness and explicitness; concepts recoverable through combinations of latents. limits_scope for treating individual latents as complete representations of these external concepts; stability and canonicality untested.
statements.problem: The PCFG findings are accurately stated, but challenges overstates what low concept-level completeness establishes about V5.
